purpose: Layout, writing-presentation and page-formation rules learned from every supplied forensic-report exemplar. The references teach structure and presentation only; case-specific facts are never reused.
sources: Azim Lalani Google Takeout Forensic Report.pdf

agent_split.report_generator_agent: Forensic content agent: artifacts, evidence selection, Objective, Procedure, Observation, Annexure and Analysis Summary.
agent_split.report_formation_agent: Formation-only agent: page packing, continuation logic, UI/PDF/DOCX parity and final document creation. It cannot rewrite content.

formation_rules: Use the saved UI section content as immutable canonical content.
Before creating a continuation page, place the next complete row, paragraph or panel on the current page when it physically fits.
Do not waste a page merely because a conservative fixed row-count threshold was reached.
Never split one table row between pages; repeat the table header after a true split.
Keep section/subsection headings with following content.
Objective/Procedure/Observation panels remain together when possible; oversized panels may continue without changing wording.
Section C must occupy remaining A4 body space: pull the next complete O/P/O card, or a meaningful prefix, onto the current page before opening a continuation.
Annexure tables must occupy remaining A4 body space only when the next rows still fit above the footer.
After packing each table page, verify every source row is present in order. A jump from serial 7 to serial 9 is a formation failure.
Place only the rows that are manageable on that A4 page. Leftover white space is required if another row would be clipped by overflow:hidden.
Never drop, shorten or rewrite Objective, Procedure or Observation text to make a page look tidy.
Only add '(CONTINUED)' as layout metadata; do not add forensic meaning or new narrative.
PDF and DOCX are generated from the same canonical content snapshot as the UI.
No export-specific sanitization, summarization or LLM rewriting is allowed.
A content fingerprint is stored with every PDF/DOCX export for parity verification.

For Introduction specifically, reproduce the formal reference-letter hierarchy: centered underlined heading, date right, compact recipient block, centered subject, body, scope/terms, and right-aligned sign-off.
Watermarks are presentation chrome only and must remain very faint (about 6-8 percent effective opacity) so they never compete with evidence text.
Pagination uses measured/estimated physical height and available printable space; a fixed 12-row threshold must not create avoidable blank areas.
reference_layout_observations: The sample reports use a stable section order: Introduction, Operating System, Artifacts, Objective/Procedure/Observation, Annexure, Analysis Summary and Appendix.
Annexure tables continue across pages while preserving serial-number continuity.
Continuation headings appear only when content truly continues onto another page.
Branding/header/footer are repeated consistently without consuming report-body facts.
The reports prefer compact pages rather than leaving usable body space empty.
Across the supplied introduction pages the heading is centered, uppercase and underlined, followed by a right-aligned date and compact formal letter blocks.
Reference watermarks are intentionally pale and sit behind content without reducing readability.
The reference pages do not use dashboard cards or exaggerated vertical spacing for the introduction letter.

content_method_sources: Azim Lalani Google Takeout Forensic Report.pdf
training_scope.rule: Review the full reference corpus before forming a report; learn document grammar and layout, never copy another case fact.

introduction_page_training.purpose: The introduction is a formal forensic transmittal/engagement letter on a dedicated A4 page.
layout: After the 44 mm letterhead band, leave approximately one normal text-line of clear space (about 4-6 mm) before the INTRODUCTION heading.
Render INTRODUCTION centered, uppercase, bold and underlined; never left-align or title-case it.
Keep the date on the upper right below the title.
Keep To and the recipient/address as a compact left-aligned block; do not stretch individual address lines vertically.
Center the Subject line; make only the Subject label visually bold when possible.
Place Dear Sir and the engagement paragraph as compact, justified letter text.
Render Scope of Work and Terms and Condition(s) as bold labels with compact numbered text immediately below.
Place Digital Forensic Analyst and company sign-off right-aligned after the terms with modest spacing, not a large empty gap.
Do not use cards, rounded borders, shadows, callouts or dashboard styling on the introduction page.
The introduction should use the body area efficiently while retaining a professional letter rhythm; do not artificially distribute blocks to fill the page.
watermark: The centered brand watermark stays behind the text and must be very faint.
Target effective watermark opacity is approximately 6-8 percent; report text must remain dominant and fully readable.
Use the same light watermark treatment in UI preview, PDF and DOCX.

page_space_training.principle: Physical remaining space, not a fixed conservative row count, decides whether the next report block can stay on the current page.
rules: Pull the next complete paragraph, table row, artifact item or O/P/O block into remaining space whenever it fits.
A half-empty annexure page that still has room for the next Social Media / Web Chat URL rows must absorb those rows instead of starting D. ANNEXURE (CONTINUED).
A table may begin in remaining page space; do not force the whole table to a new page merely because it has many rows.
Never split a single table row. Repeat the table header when the renderer creates a true continuation page.
Do not enforce a 12-row page ceiling. Estimate actual wrapped row height and use the printable body budget.
Keep headings with following content and avoid orphan Objective, Procedure or Observation labels.
Only create a continuation page when the next meaningful unit cannot physically fit or the current unit is itself oversized.
Introduction remains a dedicated formal page even if it contains some intentional white space; other report sections should not waste usable body space.

opo_page_training.purpose: Section C (Objective, Procedure & Observation) must fill each A4 body and never lose a line.
opo_page_training.learned_from: Ex-1 through Ex-5 examiner reports plus the Seger formation validation PDF.
rules: Keep a complete O/P/O card on the current page whenever its estimated height fits the remaining body.
If the next complete card does not fit but at least six units remain, place a useful prefix (title plus at least one Objective/Procedure/Observation body line) and continue the rest on the next page.
Do not leave a half-empty Section C page merely because the next card is slightly taller than the leftover gap.
Split an oversized card only as required by physical A4 capacity.
Never leave an Objective, Procedure or Observation label as the last line of a page; move the label with its first body line.
Repeat the card title on a continuation page as layout metadata only.
Every source line from every card must appear on some page. Formation may add '(continued)' but must not delete forensic text.
After the first pack, pull a following card upward when it still fits so leftover body space is used.
Estimate wrap from the actual card text width (~78 characters), not an overly narrow 56-character line that invents empty pages.

annexure_table_training.purpose: Section D (Annexure) tables must place only manageable rows on each A4 page and never lose a row.
annexure_table_training.learned_from: Ex-1 through Ex-5 examiner reports plus the Seger formation validation PDF.
rules: Keep packing rows onto the current page only while estimated wrapped height still fits above the footer and page number.
A wrapping 5-column URL table may hold at most 5 data rows with its title and preview note, or 6 rows on a continuation page.
A 4-column Objective/Procedure/Observation table (Analysis Summary) may hold at most 2 tall rows on a page.
Do not cap a tall observation row at 6 units. Use the real wrapped height up to 16 units so a third row is not packed under the footer.
After every pack, check that every source row appears in order. Missing serials (for example 7 then 9, skipping 8) must fail closed and re-pack.
If another row would enter the letterhead footer, start the section (CONTINUED) with that row. Do not clip it.
Never split one table row. Repeat the table header and '(continued)' only on a true continuation page.
Every source row from every annexure table must appear on some page, in order.
Do not invent filler rows or drop URLs to make a page look tidy.
Leftover white space is acceptable; missing content is not.

content_parity_training.rule: UI, PDF and DOCX use one canonical saved section snapshot.
